correctness.rationale: The complete bitmask/permutation orbit census covers 52 unlabeled simple graphs on 1–5 vertices, with orbit totals 1,099 labeled graphs; every multipath face is checked by a finite recursive exact predicate. All faceposet Morse matchings are explicitly Hasse-acyclic. Unimodular unit pivots leave only one nonzero residual row (2,2,2) in the witness degree-2 boundary, whose gcd is 2; the critical ranks give H1=Z/2,H2=Z7. An opposite arc-order matching gives residual (2,-2). Independent direct enumeration of all 2^14 witness arc subsets and unreduced simplicial modular ranks over F2 and F3, including boundary-square-zero, confirm the interpretation. A separate full raw integer Smith computation gave d1 units^13, d2 units^40 and 2, d3 units^12.

value.rationale: The motivating 2022 paper asks about the extent and origin of torsion in multipath complexes. The exact smallest number of underlying vertices and uniqueness of the exception is a natural sharp boundary and useful classification, not a parameter-arbitrary numerical invariant. The three-page triangular book is a canonical graph. It strengthens known six-vertex torsion examples, supplies the complete H1/H2 integral invariant, and makes a reproducible benchmark for directed-topology torsion. No arbitrary orientations or infinite-family theorem is asserted.
